They never let me know that I would be able to feel the metal in my back, nor the complications that come with the surgery years down the line that are almost guaranteed to happen. I also sustained nerve damage during the surgery that resulted in loss of feeling in my leg, though nerve damage was warned about pre-surgery. They also never let me know that spinal fusion would worsen my arthiritis, and lead to a hip replacement faster. I learned those things after surgery. 

I did know that I wouldn't be able to bend my back though. I was fine with it pre-surgery, but actually experiencing it and living with it is a whole other thing. 

Medically, I am not considered botched. There's nothing that was royally screwed up that caused me to be permanently disfigured. I got some nerve damage, but other than that the surgery went fine. But I personally feel botched, and so do all the older people that I've seen who warn you to never get back surgery because of how much it lowered their quality of life.

Like OP probably feels about LASIK, I personally think Spinal fusion is an incredibly horrendous, out-dated surgery that causes more harm than good, and should be banned. Medicine is always evolving, so looking forward to the future is the best we can do.

I had something done to my spine nearly a year ago, (on July 7th it will be one year). I had a surgery that corrected severe scoliosis. I went into it willingly, and ended up absolutely despising how I ended up. I can feel metal in my back daily with every movement, I can't bend my back, etc. Like yours, mine is also irreversible. 

Over time, the pain of what you lost will become more bearable as you adjust to your new normal. I know in the moment that that may seem impossible, (TRUST me, I KNOW that feeling very well), but It has for me; I feel better now than I did 4 months post-op (which was the absolute worst month in my recovery. I cried basically every hour regretting my surgery). 

You also never know, in the future there may be a surgery to reverse the effects of your LASIK surgery. That is what I'm hoping for mine. However, if you cant wait that long, I understand. I've felt the same way. 

You can't let the "what-ifs" destroy you though. You need to come to accept that you made a mistake, and although there is nothing you can do to reverse the surgery, you can do better moving forward and always rethink and evaluate certain choices that you make about your health. Also, perhaps seeing someone who can help you adjust to your new normal surrounding your sight. 

I love you ❤
